prerequisites: All courses that provide technical knowledge and sector-specific competencies.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability for the drafting, signing, and development of projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability for project direction and management.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

syllabus_topics: Concept of project and its relationship with its environment
Studies with their own entity (environmental impact studies, health and safety in the project)
Technical and economic-financial viability. Risk management.
Responsibility and attributions in the project scope
Trends and future of project management
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum of 35% of the maximum possible score must be obtained in the "written tests". Unpassed recoverable parts can be re-examined in subsequent calls, except for "oral tests" and "works and projects" which occur once per academic year. If a student fails the ordinary call and has less than 50% of the maximum possible score in the non-recoverable parts, then in subsequent calls, the "written tests" score must exceed 50% of its maximum possible. For part-time students, non-recoverable activities may be replaced by similar activities or equivalent evaluation tests, provided the reason for non-completion is the same for which the university granted part-time student status. If the critical evaluation criteria are not met, the final grade will be "FAIL", with the sum of obtained scores capped at 4.5 points.
